segments.x: [Music] I love spray painting. I I can't get enough of it. It's about [—] graffiti. It's about destroying public property, changing your environment, creating the environment that you live in. It's up on the walls. It's everywhere.
It's free. So, I'm trying to work on like a two-handed technique. It's mine for the taking. It's like stealing. Dave has nine lives and he can do a lot of things. Get away from it.

I just wanted to destroy [—] I just wanted to like make [—] funny. [Music] Heat. We're rich and so I just start stealing. I'm like, why the [—] do these people get to deserve to have all this stuff? I had a whole Robin Hood thing going on.
David was a standout from the minute I had him as a student. He didn't do a lot of preliminary. He just like wham. He just went for it. Kind of a Renaissance guy in a way.

They're completely shitty, but in a good way. Today we have a true maverick, a renegade street artist, David Choe. I get paid to doodle, draw. [Music] His style is the dirty style. You know, his style is just dirty.

A wall maybe 70, 80 ft long. And David painted everything on this wall with a full range of color and effects. It's a beautiful almost tapestry like treatment of this gigantic wall. [Music] No one's handed him anything. He's worked hard for everything. He just did everything to make that happen for himself.

His shirts sold really well because there's stuff in his art that people can relate to. [Music] David's genius is somewhat about being a bad boy. One day when people stop buying my paintings, quit wearing my t-shirts, I could still rob your [—] house.

Here's some fan mail. Here's some hate mail. Touching a nerve somewhere. Everything I've ever done in my life that I enjoyed, I do it like to the extreme. [Music] I travel a hell of a lot. I travel all the [—] time. It's like no big deal.

Like I traveled to Japan a month before I went to Japan again. I feel like Godzilla when I go over there. I mean, especially in Tokyo where there's like I want to steal everything, you know? When I got to the airport, I was like, maybe I shouldn't get on that plane. Instead, I got on the plane, got arrested in less

than 24 hours, and spent the next 3 months in jail. This is going to be a dark time in my life. Now, my girlfriend lives a righteous life. She ends up in a brand new home. I slee and slime my way through life, and I end up in a cell. It was really like I was

getting caught for like my lifetime of, you know, everything that happened. I have to unlearn like my whole life. I've been taking time apart from her. Spent too much time apart. She doesn't feel it anymore.

She thinks I'm a liar. It's over, dude. Prison life changes your perspective on things, you know? I've always like spray painted Bible verses of like irreverent [—] from the Bible. I had that copy of the Bible and I would, you know, write down certain verses in this. Look at your life. Like the stuff you're into,
like who are you? Like what do you believe in? Like what are you about? Every aspect of how I live my life is illegal. I can't go on like this. I mean, I can't live like this anymore.

It's been really strange trying to make a living as an artist when you really don't care about your life and you're on this path of self-destruction. He's like some classic hero going through a series of life passages. He got to one where he had to leave behind some older traits.

Now that I have a stronger focus in my life, I'm leaving it up to a higher being. If I can bring hope into anyone's lives, great. [Applause] [Music] [Applause] I always use Dave as an example of the impossible to fail spirit.
I know he still has this inner struggle, which means that he still has good art in him. I guess there's a lot of [—] that I didn't have to go through to get to where I am now.
This is the [—] life of a [—] [—] ass tortured artist. [Applause] [Music] [Applause]

editorial.description: An unofficial *Dirty Hands* trailer introduces Choe through spray paint, graffiti, paid drawing and the label ‘dirty style,’ then previews Japan, illegality, exhaustion with his way of living and friends' belief that unresolved struggle feeds the work.
